info.title: Bitcoin Address Activity Explorer API
info.description: Unusual-activity scoring for Bitcoin addresses, from Assignment 2's models. A flag means unusual for this address's own history, nothing more.

get.description: Answers 200 once the models are loaded, and 503 while they load. Never cached: the front end polls it.

Addresses with enough history come first, busiest first; the short-history ones follow.

get.summary: A filtered, sorted page of transaction rows
get.description:
Filter by one day (`date`) or a range (`from`, `to`), by `status` and `direction` (each may repeat), sort by
`time`, `amount` (the size of the net amount, in or out) or `score` (a leading minus reverses), and page with `page` and `pageSize`.
A filter that matches nothing is a 200 with an empty list.

get.summary: One transaction: facts, features, reason and every method's verdict
get.description:
The transaction's facts, its four features with their usual values and z-scores, what each was compared with,
the template's explanation and every method's score and flag. 404 `unsupported` for an address outside the
snapshot, 404 `not_found` when the transaction is not that address's, and 422 `insufficient_history`, with the
transaction's facts, when too little earlier history lay behind it to score it.

post.summary: A hypothetical transaction's verdict from every model that can score it
post.description:
Scores a transaction of `amountBtc` BTC, `direction` in or out, at `time`, against the address's real history
strictly before that time. Nothing is stored. 400 names each field at fault; 404 `unsupported` for an address outside
the snapshot; 422 when too little history lay before the time, with the counts and the first day that can be scored.

post.summary: Scores over a range of amounts, from one feature build
post.description:
The same hypothetical transaction at many amounts: `amountsBtc` (up to `curveMaxPoints`), or `minBtc`, `maxBtc` and
`points` spaced on a log scale, or neither, for `curvePoints` amounts from a hundredth to a thousand times the
address's usual amount in that direction. Each method answers one score and one flag per amount; the scores equal
what E8 gives for each amount alone. Errors as E8.

get.summary: The scored transactions as a CSV or JSON file
get.description:
The rows E6 would list for the same filters, all of them, in the order asked for. `format` is `csv` (the default;
UTF-8, a header row, amounts in BTC, text guarded against formulas) or `json`. A flagged row carries the limitation line.

get.summary: The methods, their thresholds and test results
get.description:
For each method: its family, what its score measures, the score it flags at, whether it can score a new
transaction, and Assignment 2's test results (mean recall and recall per planted pattern, each with its 95%
interval, and the flag rate on real transactions). The numbers are read from Assignment 2's evaluation tables.
